agent: wave 11 agent A - the evaluation half of the event script language
question: CEventScope's layout; slot 6 (Evaluate) for CAndTrigger, COrTrigger, CNotTrigger and CContextTrigger; how CContextTrigger rebinds the scope; whether trigger evaluation is cached (slots 10 and 11).

addresses.name: CAndTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**AND over the child list, and nothing else.** 0x5D06E0 to two `ret 4` exits at 0x5D070A (all children passed) and 0x5D0712 (one did not); `je 0x5D070D` from inside jumps past the first, so it is one function, not two (trap 3). It walks `children_first (+0x8)` - payload at node+0, next at node+8 - and calls each child's **slot 6** through `[vftable+0x18]`, stopping at the first `al == 0`. An empty child list returns **true**. It reads no field but `+0x8` and allocates nothing.

**It holds no cached answer**: there is no memo field, no dirty flag and no early exit other than the first failing child, so every call re-walks the whole subtree. With 100,464 live CAndTriggers that is the whole cost model of the trigger forest.

**Extent, trap 2:** `image.functionStart(0x9D06E0)` answers 0x9D06C0, because CTrigger::CountEvaluation ends `ret 0xC` at 0x5D06DD with **no padding at all** before this prologue. The upper boundary is clean (11 `int3`, then CAndTrigger::GetBlockText at 0x5D0720); the lower one is an abutment, and the vftable is what settles it - CAndTrigger's table (VA 0x15B589C) holds 0x9D06E0 at slot 6.

**Two holders**, CAndTrigger and CMTTHModifier slot 6 - and CMTTHModifier derives from CAndTrigger, so that is inheritance and not a linker fold (trap 4). It means a mean-time-to-happen modifier's conditions are an AND-tree re-evaluated the same way.
addresses.evidence: Read instruction by instruction, 0x9D06E0..0x9D0712. `mov esi,[ecx+8]` is the already-recorded children_first; `[eax+0x18]` is slot 6 (0x18/4 = 6) and vtable.py confirms CAndTrigger slot 6 == 0x9D06E0. retsBefore(0x9D06E0, 0x9D0720) returns two `ret 4`, both this function's. Shown wrong by: a field read other than +0x8 in the body, or CAndTrigger's table slot 6 not being this address.

addresses.name: COrTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**OR over the child list.** 0x5D0D00 to two `ret 4` at 0x5D0D2A (nothing matched) and 0x5D0D32 (something did). Instruction for instruction CAndTrigger::Evaluate with the test and the two return values swapped: it stops at the first child whose slot 6 answers `al == 1` and returns true, and an **empty child list returns false**. Reads only `children_first (+0x8)`; no cache, no allocation.

Note the asymmetry in the bytes: the AND tests `test al,al / je`, the OR tests `cmp al,1 / je`. For a bool that is the same question, but it is what is written.

**Extent, trap 2:** functionStart(0x9D0D00) answers 0x9D0CD0 - CAndTrigger::CountEvaluation ends `ret 0xC` at 0x5D0CFD with no padding. Settled by COrTrigger's table (VA 0x15F7C4C) slot 6. Upper boundary clean: 11 `int3`, then COrTrigger::GetBlockText at 0x5D0D40.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D0D00..0x9D0D32. vtable.py: COrTrigger slot 6 == 0x9D0D00, one holder. retsBefore returns the two `ret 4` of this body. Shown wrong by the empty-list return being true, or by any field other than +0x8 being read.

addresses.name: CNotTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**NOR over the child list, not a one-child negation.** 0x5D12C0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5D12EA (true) and 0x5D12F2 (false). The same loop again: it calls each child's slot 6 and returns **false** as soon as one answers 1; if none does - including when there are no children at all - it returns **true**. So `NOT = { a b }` is `!(a || b)`, and with the single child the scripts actually write it is plain negation. Reads only `children_first (+0x8)`; no cache.

12 `int3` before the entry and 11 after the exit, so both boundaries are clean here.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D12C0..0x9D12F2. vtable.py: CNotTrigger slot 6 == 0x9D12C0, one holder. functionStart agrees with the entry. Shown wrong by the loop breaking after the first child rather than on the first true one.

addresses.name: CContextTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**The scope switch: an AND whose children see a different CEventScope.** 0x5D1530 to two `ret 4` at 0x5D155A (false) and 0x5D1583 (true).

    sub esp, 0x4c                    ; a 0x48-byte CEventScope at esp+8, which is exactly the frame
    CEventScope::MakeScope(scope, this + 0x40, &local)
    if (local.resolved (+0x3C) == 0) return false
    for each child: if (!child->Evaluate(&local)) return false
    return true

`this + 0x40` is CContextTrigger's own data - CTrigger is 0x40 bytes - and is the 0x110-byte scope specification its constructor copies in. `[esp+0x44]` is the local scope's `+0x3C`, the `resolved` flag CEventScope's constructor sets to 1 and MakeScope clears when the context names nothing.

**So an unresolvable context is false, not an error**: `owner = { ... }` on a province nobody owns, or `ally = { ... }` for a country with no entry in the list MakeScope draws from, makes the whole block fail quietly.

**And the new scope is a stack temporary built per evaluation.** Nothing is memoised: each call copies the parent scope (18 dword moves, CEventScope::CopyConstruct) and re-runs the whole resolver, which for the `ally` and `local_enemy` contexts means an `operator new` and a `free` for a std::vector of candidate tags **every time the trigger is evaluated**. With 10,974 live CContextTriggers that is the one place in the trigger forest where evaluation touches the heap.

9 `int3` before the entry, 10 after the exit; CContextTrigger::GetBlockText follows at 0x5D1590.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D1530..0x9D1583. The frame arithmetic pins the local: `and esp,-8; sub esp,0x4c; push esi` puts the object at esp+8 and 8+0x48 = 0x50 = the whole frame, and [esp+0x44] is object+0x3C, the same byte CEventScope's constructor writes as `mov word [eax+0x3c],1`. vtable.py: CContextTrigger slot 6 == 0x9D1530, one holder. Shown wrong by MakeScope writing its result anywhere but esp+8, or by [esp+0x44] not being object+0x3C.

addresses.name: CTrigger::WalkChildren
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTrigger::WalkChildren(CTrigger* this, void* collector, CEventScope* scope, bool polarity, int weight)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 10, the base body: forward the whole argument list to every child and do nothing else.** 0x5D0680 to the single `ret 0x10` at 0x5D06B1. 143 of the 164 trigger classes inherit it, so on a leaf trigger with no children it is a no-op.

**The argument list, corrected.** `project.json` recorded this slot as `(this, CEventScope* scope, int* unknown, int* passed, int* total)`. The count is right - `ret 0x10`, four stack arguments - and the order is not. The scope is the **second**: CContextTrigger::WalkChildren (0x5D2470) rebinds `[ebp+0xC]` and passes the new scope in that position while passing `[ebp+8]` through untouched, and CExistsTrigger's own slot 10 (0x5DABA0) calls `this->Evaluate([ebp+0xC])`. The last two are not counters either: COrTrigger's override divides `[ebp+0x14]` by `children_count (+0x10)`, clamps it to at least 1 and passes that down - an int split among the branches, i.e. a **weight** - and CNotTrigger's override replaces `[ebp+0x10]` with `(byte == 0)`, i.e. a **polarity bool** it inverts.

**What it is for.** A leaf's override reports itself: CExistsTrigger's is `if (polarity && this->Evaluate(scope)) collect(collector, weight, this->+0x44, this->+0x48)` through rva 0x4A5270, which inserts into a map owned by a **CAIStrategy** (its destructor is rva 0x4A3880). So slot 10 is the AI's weighted attribution walk over a trigger tree - which country or province this condition argues for, and how strongly - and not an evaluation helper. The name describes this body rather than the overrides; it is kept because that is what `project.json` already calls the slot.

**Extent, trap 2:** functionStart(0x9D0680) answers 0x9D0663, which is in the middle of an instruction - the previous function ends `ret 0x10` at 0x9D067D..0x9D067F and this prologue is the very next byte, so the backward walk never saw a boundary. retsBefore(0x9D0680, 0x9D06C0) returns exactly one `ret`, and CTrigger's RTTI `introduces` list gives slot 10 as 0x9D0680.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D0680..0x9D06B1, and the four overrides (0x9D1270, 0x9D1340, 0x9D2470, 0x9DABA0) that give the arguments their meaning. `[eax+0x28]` is slot 10 (0x28/4 = 10). The argument order rests on CContextTrigger::WalkChildren substituting at position 2 and on CExistsTrigger passing position 2 to slot 6; shown wrong by either of those reading a different stack slot. 143 holders, all slot 10, all deriving from CTrigger - inheritance, not a fold.

addresses.name: CTrigger::CountEvaluation
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTrigger::CountEvaluation(CTrigger* this, CEventScope* scope, int* passed, int* total)
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D06C0..0x9D06DD, 10 instructions. `ret 0xC` = three stack arguments for a __thiscall, which is what the recorded signature predicts. CTrigger's RTTI introduces slot 11 at 0x9D06C0. Shown wrong by the slot-6 call being on a child rather than on `this`.

addresses.name: CAndTrigger::CountEvaluation
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAndTrigger::CountEvaluation(CAndTrigger* this, CEventScope* scope, int* passed, int* total)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 11 over the children: how many of this AND's conditions are met.** 0x5D0CD0 to the single `ret 0xC` at 0x5D0CFD. It walks `children_first (+0x8)` and calls each child's **slot 11** - `[eax+0x2c]`, 0x2C/4 = 11 - forwarding all three arguments unchanged, so the counters accumulate over the whole subtree. It never calls slot 6 itself; the leaves do.

That is the `n of m conditions met` figure the trigger tooltip shows, and it costs a **second** full evaluation of every leaf under the block.

7 `int3` before the entry; it abuts COrTrigger::Evaluate at 0x5D0D00 with none after (trap 2 for that function, not for this one).

**Eight holders**, all slot 11: CAndTrigger, CAnyCoreTrigger, CAnyNeighborCountryTrigger, CAnyNeighborProvinceTrigger, CAnyOwnedProvinceTrigger, CEnemyScopeTrigger, CMTTHModifier and CRegionScopeTrigger. All eight derive from CAndTrigger, so this is inheritance and not a linker fold (trap 4).
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D0CD0..0x9D0CFD. mergeFindings.inTables() gives the eight holders and they all share CAndTrigger as an ancestor. Shown wrong by the dispatch displacement being anything but 0x2C.

addresses.name: COrTrigger::CountEvaluation
addresses.signature: void __thiscall COrTrigger::CountEvaluation(COrTrigger* this, CEventScope* scope, int* passed, int* total)
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D1230..0x9D1267. `inc dword [eax]` on [ebp+0x10] before the loop and on [ebp+0xC] inside it fixes which pointer is which against CTrigger::CountEvaluation, where `passed` is [ebp+0xC] and `total` is [ebp+0x10]. One holder, COrTrigger slot 11.

addresses.name: COrTrigger::WalkChildren
addresses.signature: void __thiscall COrTrigger::WalkChildren(COrTrigger* this, void* collector, CEventScope* scope, bool polarity, int weight)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 10 for an OR: split the weight between the branches.** 0x5D1270 to the single `ret 0x10` at 0x5D12B1.

    share = weight / this->children_count (+0x10)      ; signed idiv
    if (share < 1) share = 1
    for each child: child->WalkChildren(collector, scope, polarity, share)

This is what identifies the fourth argument of slot 10 as a weight rather than the depth the slot-9 signature of the same shape carries: nothing else would be divided by the number of children.

**It divides by `children_count` without testing it for zero** - an `or = { }` with no children would raise a divide-by-zero here. The loader never builds one, so this is a note about the body and not a reachable fault. 6 `int3` before the entry, 12 after.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D1270..0x9D12B1. `idiv dword [ecx+0x10]` is the already-recorded children_count, and `[eax+0x28]` is slot 10. One holder, COrTrigger slot 10. Shown wrong by [ecx+0x10] not being the child count.

addresses.name: CNotTrigger::WalkChildren
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNotTrigger::WalkChildren(CNotTrigger* this, void* collector, CEventScope* scope, bool polarity, int weight)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 10 for a NOT: flip the polarity and hand the same weight down.** 0x5D1340 to the single `ret 0x10` at 0x5D1375.

    flipped = (polarity == 0)                 ; cmp byte [ebp+0x10], 0 ; sete bl
    for each child: child->WalkChildren(collector, scope, flipped, weight)

This is what identifies the third argument of slot 10 as a bool: it is read as a byte, compared with zero and passed on as the result of that comparison. A leaf's override uses it as `report only if set` - see CExistsTrigger at 0x5DABA0 - so under an odd number of NOTs a satisfied condition is **not** reported to the collector. 15 `int3` before the entry, 8 after.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D1340..0x9D1375. `cmp byte ptr [ebp+0x10], 0; sete bl` then `push ebx` in the third argument position. One holder, CNotTrigger slot 10.

addresses.name: CNotTrigger::CountEvaluation
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNotTrigger::CountEvaluation(CNotTrigger* this, CEventScope* scope, int* passed, int* total)
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D1380..0x9D13D0. The locals are initialised to zero at 0x5D138C/0x5D1393 and the arithmetic at 0x5D13C0-0x5D13CB is `eax = innerTotal; edx = eax - innerPassed; *[ebp+0xC] += edx; *[ebp+0x10] += eax`. One holder, CNotTrigger slot 11.

addresses.name: CContextTrigger::WalkChildren
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CContextTrigger::WalkChildren(CContextTrigger* this, void* collector, CEventScope* scope, bool polarity, int weight)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 10 for a context: rebind the scope, then run the base body with it.** 0x5D2470 to the single `ret 0x10` at 0x5D24B0. The same 0x48-byte stack scope and the same `resolved (+0x3C)` gate as CContextTrigger::Evaluate, and then a **direct** call to CTrigger::WalkChildren (0x5D0680) with the new scope substituted for argument 2 and the other three passed through.

This is the body that fixes slot 10's argument order: `ecx` for MakeScope comes from `[ebp+0xC]`, and `[ebp+8]` is pushed on unchanged. 9 `int3` before the entry, 13 after.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D2470..0x9D24B0. The call at 0x5D24A7 is a direct `call 0x9D0680`, not a virtual dispatch, so the base body is reached whatever the subclass. One holder, CContextTrigger slot 10.

addresses.name: CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation(CContextTrigger* this, CEventScope* scope, int* passed, int* total)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 11 for a context.** 0x5D24C0 to the single `ret 0xC` at 0x5D250D. It builds the rebound 0x48-byte stack scope exactly as Evaluate does and then walks the children calling their **slot 11** with it, forwarding `passed` and `total`.

**It does not test `resolved (+0x3C)`**, which CContextTrigger::Evaluate and CContextTrigger::WalkChildren both do - so when the context names nothing the tooltip counts the children against a scope the evaluator would have refused. That is a difference between the displayed tally and the answer, and it is in the bytes rather than inferred. CContextTrigger::GetBlockText does not test it either, so the split is between the two simulation-side slots and the two display-side ones. 13 `int3` before the entry; it abuts the next function at 0x5D2510.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D24C0..0x9D250D, all 20 instructions: there is no `cmp byte [esp+...], 0` after the `call 0x9C1C10` at 0x5D24DA, whereas 0x5D154D and 0x5D248D both have one. CContextTrigger::GetBlockText (0x5D1590 to 0x5D2466) was decoded end to end and holds no read of +0x3C at all. Shown wrong by finding such a test anywhere in either body.

addresses.name: CEventScope::MakeScope
addresses.signature: CEventScope* __thiscall CEventScope::MakeScope(CEventScope* this, CEventScopeSpec* spec, CEventScope* out)
addresses.comment:
**The whole of scope rebinding - what `owner = { ... }`, `FROM = { ... }` or a bare country tag actually does.** 0x5C1C10 to four `ret 8` at 0x5C1C85, 0x5C1E03, 0x5C1F6A and 0x5C1FD4; all four restore the same SEH slot `[esp+0x84]` and the body has one prologue, so it is one function (trap 3). 14 `int3` before the entry, 9 after the last exit. Eight callers: CContextTrigger slots 6, 9, 10 and 11, CTrigger::LoadKey (0x5CAE96), and three in the effect loader at 0x59E2C8/0x59E337/0x59E635.

`spec` is the 0x110-byte scope specification a CContextTrigger keeps at `this + 0x40`: a SaveToken at +0, the key's text as 0x100 bytes at +4, a literal province id at +0x104 and a literal CCountryTag at +0x108/+0x10C. It is left as `void*` because `project.json` has no struct for it yet; EventScopeSpec_Construct (0x5C1B30) is what fills it.

It **copies the receiver into `out` first** (CEventScope::CopyConstruct), so the new scope inherits the random state, the seed, `rebel_faction`, both `from_*` fields and - crucially - `this_scope (+0x38)` unchanged, and the cases below then overwrite only `country` and `province`. That is the rebinding mechanism in one sentence.

Then, in order:

- `spec->+0x10C != 0`, i.e. the key was a country tag the database knows: `out->country = spec->+0x108/+0x10C`, `out->province = 0`. This is the `GER = { ... }` form, and it is tested **before** the token switch.
- otherwise a switch on `spec->token`:

| token | id | what it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (number) | 0xC | `province = spec->+0x104`, `country = "---"` - a bare province id |
| `owner` | 0x1EC | `country` = `g_CMap (0x1A8557C) ->+0x2200 [province] ->owner (+0x32C)`, `province = 0` |
| `controller` | 0x1ED | the same province's `controller (+0x334)`, `province = 0` |
| `from` | 0x34F | `country = from_country (+0x18)`, `province = from_province (+0x30)` |
| `ally` | 0x359 | a **random** entry of the CList at `CCountry +0xF88` of `country_id`'s country |
| `this` | 0x377 | `country` and `province` of `this_scope (+0x38)`, then returns at once |
| `capital_scope` | 0x3B4 | `province` = that country's `acting_capital_province_id (+0xE24)`, `country = "---"` |
| `sea_zone` | 0x3E8 | `province` = `province->path_node_ptr (+0xD4) ->+0xA4`, `country = "---"` |
| `local_enemy` | 0x621 | a **random** owner tag among the units in the province (`CMapProvince::units +0x2B8`) whose `combats_count (+0x11C) > 0` and whose `owner_id (+0x128)` is not the province's owner |
| `overlord` | 0x631 | that country's `faction_leader_tag (+0xF38)`, `province = 0` |
| anything else | - | sets `out->unknown_context (+0x3D) = 1` and falls into the empty-candidate arm |

The two random cases build a `std::vector<CCountryTag>` on the stack with an `operator new`, pick an element with `(rand(&this->random_state) % count)` through the LCG at rva 0x6A2E90, and free it - **per call**, so those two context keywords are the only ones in the language that touch the heap to be evaluated. When the vector comes up empty, 0x5C1F34 clears `out->resolved (+0x3C)`, which is the flag every caller but CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation then refuses on.

Two tokens, 0xC and 0xF, are **not in the compiled token table** at all; so are the other low lexer ids 7, 10, 13, 14, 15 and 19. 0xF is the one EventScopeSpec_Construct tests before trying the text as a country tag and 0xC is the one this switch answers with the literal province id, so they are the identifier and number classes of the lexer rather than save keys. That part is inference.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end, 0x9C1C10..0x9C1FD4. The token ids are decoded from the comparison chain and resolved against ghidra/saveTokens.json, and every one of the nine that is in the table names a field the record already holds under the matching name - owner/controller are CMapProvince +0x32C/+0x334, capital_scope is CCountry::acting_capital_province_id, overlord is CCountry::faction_leader_tag, local_enemy walks CMapProvince::units testing CUnit::combats_count and CUnit::owner_id. Nine independent agreements is the control. `ret 8` with the spec at [ebp+8] and the out pointer at [ebp+0xC] is read off the two push orders at all eight call sites. Shown wrong by any of those field names disagreeing, or by the out pointer being at [ebp+8].

addresses.name: CEventScope::CEventScope
addresses.signature: CEventScope* __stdcall CEventScope::CEventScope(CEventScope* this@EAX, int seed@EDX, int unknown@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment:
**The CEventScope constructor, and the authority on the object's size.** 0x5C1610 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5C167F, 7 `int3` before and 14 after; CEventScope::SaveContents follows at 0x5C1690. It is called out of line at 40 sites and inlined at many more - the daily event pass (0x5C0A40) has a copy at 0x5C0A80-0x5C0ABC.

A register convention: `this` arrives in **EAX** and is used before it is written, the seed in **EDX**, one value on the stack, and EAX comes back unchanged so callers use it as the return - CTrigger::LoadKey does `mov ecx, eax` straight after. Hence the explicit storage on every parameter.

It writes, in this order: `+0 = vftable (VA 0x15B8AEC)`, `+4 = 0x18D` (the CPersistent `none` token), `+8 = 1` (dead - overwritten at the end), `+0x10 = 0x2D2D2D` (`"---"`), `+0x18 = 0x2D2D2D`, `+0x40 = [ebp+8]`, then zeroes `+0x24`, `+0x14`, `+0x1C`, `+0x34`, `+0x44`, `+0x28`, `+0x30`, `+0x20`, sets `word +0x3C = 1` (so `resolved = 1`, `unknown_context = 0`), `+0x2C = seed`, **`+0x38 = this`**, and finally `+8 = seed` and `+0xC = seed`.

The highest field it touches is `+0x44`, which with CEventScope::CopyConstruct's +4..+0x44 makes the object **0x48 bytes** - `project.json`'s `size` of `0x38` is wrong, and the comment on `+0x34` in the same record already says 0x48.

`+0x38 = this` is the one to keep: it means the `this` context always resolves, and since the copy constructor copies the pointer verbatim, a rebound scope still points at the scope the event was raised with.

The stack argument lands in `+0x40` and is 0 at 28 of the 29 call sites inspected; `0x474501` is the exception and passes its own `[ebp+0xc]`. Left unnamed.
addresses.evidence: Read all 27 instructions. `this` in EAX is settled by `mov dword [eax+4], 0x18d` being the second instruction of the body with no write to EAX before it. The seed in EDX is settled by two call sites, 0x4B9A99 and 0x5769A0, which do `call 0xAA2F80; mov edx, eax` immediately before. The inlined copy inside RunDailyEventPass independently confirms the offsets: project.json already says that function leaves days_in_month zero at 0x5C0AAD, and 0x5C0AAD writes [ebp-0x3C], which on that frame is scope+0x34. Shown wrong by a write past +0x44, or by the copy constructor copying more than +4..+0x44.

addresses.name: CEventScope::CopyConstruct
addresses.comment:
**Copy one CEventScope over another, field by field, and the second witness that the object is 0x48 bytes.** 0x3C850 to the bare `ret` at 0x3C8C4, 5 `int3` after; 51 sites in the image reference the vftable constant it writes and this is the out-of-line copy they share.

It writes the vftable (VA 0x15B8AEC) and then copies **+4 through +0x44** - sixteen dwords and the two bytes at +0x3C and +0x3D, read with `movzx` one at a time, which is how we know `resolved` and `unknown_context` are two separate bools rather than the word the constructor writes them as. Nothing past +0x44 is touched, and nothing before +4.

Both arguments are in registers and there is no stack to clean, hence the bare `ret` and the explicit storage. It copies `this_scope (+0x38)` **verbatim**, which is what makes a rebound scope still resolve `this` to the original.
addresses.evidence: Read all 29 instructions. The highest offset written is +0x44 and the sequence is contiguous from +4, so the size is 0x48 on this body alone, independently of the constructor. Shown wrong by a copy of +0x48 or beyond anywhere in the image.

addresses.name: CEventScope::SaveContents
addresses.comment:
**Slot 2, and the key-by-key authority on CEventScope's layout.** 0x5C1690 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5C1889, 4 `int3` before CEventScope::LoadKey at 0x5C1890. Every field is written only when it is non-zero, in this order:

| guard | key | written from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x14 != 0` | `country` (0x24D) | the string at `+0x10` |
| `+0x28 != 0` | `province` (0x1EE) | `+0x28` as a number |
| `+0x1C != 0` | `from_country` (0x61B) | the string at `+0x18` |
| `+0x30 != 0` | `from_province` (0x61C) | `+0x30` as a number |
| `+0x20 != 0 \|\| +0x24 != 0` | `rebel_faction` (0x644) | the object-id pair at `+0x20`, through rva 0x6789F0 |
| always | `seed` (0x356) | `+0x2C` as a number |

So six of CEventScope's fourteen dwords are persisted and the other eight - the random state at +8/+0xC, `days_in_month`, `this_scope`, the two flags, +0x40 and +0x44 - are runtime only. That is the matching half of CEventScope::LoadKey (0x5C1890), which switches on the same six tokens and writes the same six offsets.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end. Each `mov ecx, <token>; call SaveWriteKey (0x67A1B0)` is immediately followed by the write of the field it guards, and the six tokens resolve through ghidra/saveTokens.json to the six names above. CEventScope::LoadKey's switch, decoded separately, writes exactly the same six offsets for the same six tokens - an independent agreement. One holder, CEventScope slot 2. Shown wrong by a seventh key anywhere in the body.

addresses.name: EventScope_GetCountryTag
addresses.comment:
**"Which country is this scope about", resolved through `this_scope`.** 0x5C1A40 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5C1B1F, 3 `int3` before and 14 after.

    s = scope->this_scope (+0x38)
    if (s->country_id (+0x14) != 0 || s->province (+0x28) == 0)
        *out = s->country (+0x10)
    else
        *out = g_CCurrentGameState (0x1A89790) ->+0xB8C [s->province] ->owner (+0x32C)
    return out

So a scope that names only a province still answers with a country - the province's owner - and a scope that names neither answers `"---"` with id 0. It reaches the scope **only** through `+0x38`, which is the clearest single piece of evidence for what that field is: the constructor sets it to `this`, so for an unrebound scope this reads the scope itself.

Class-free on purpose (trap 11): the scope is a stack argument, `ecx` is never read, and the out pointer arrives in **EDI**, so no ordinary `__thiscall` describes it.
addresses.evidence: Read all 48 instructions. The caller that identifies the argument is CExistsTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DABE0), whose [ebp+8] is the CEventScope - the branch beside this call reads [ebp+8]+0x18/+0x1C, which is `from_country`, directly. `lea edi, [esp+0x1c]` immediately before the call is the out slot. Shown wrong by any caller passing something that is not a CEventScope.

addresses.name: EventScopeSpec_Construct
addresses.comment:
**Build the 0x110-byte scope specification a CContextTrigger carries, from the parsed key.** 0x5C1B30 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5C1BFF, 14 `int3` on both sides.

    memcpy(out, source, 0x104)                   ; rep movsd, 0x41 dwords
    out->+0x104 = 0; out->+0x108 = "---"; out->+0x10C = 0
    if (atoi(out + 4) != 0)   out->+0x104 = atoi(out + 4)
    else if (out->+0 == 0xF)  CCountryDataBase::GetTag(db, &out->+0x108, out + 4)

So the 0x104-byte head it copies is `{ SaveToken token; char text[0x100]; }` - the parse context's current token, taken from `CParseContext + 0x20` by CTrigger::LoadKey - and this function derives the two literal forms from the text: a province id when the text is a number, a country tag when the text is a word (token 0xF) the country database knows. The country database is get-or-created here, 0x57C bytes through CCountryDataBase::CCountryDataBase (rva 0x24D0) on the singleton at 0x1A855A4.

`source` arrives in EDX and `out` on the stack, so the convention is explicit. Also called as the copy constructor of the member, from CContextTrigger::CContextTrigger at 0x5D150E.

**The struct wants a name in `project.json`.** There is no RTTI class for it and `mergeFindings` will not create a struct, so `void*` here and in CEventScope::MakeScope is a placeholder.
addresses.evidence: Read all 40 instructions. `mov ecx, 0x41; rep movsd` is 0x104 bytes exactly, and the three fields written after it are the three CEventScope::MakeScope reads (+0x104, +0x108, +0x10C) - two functions agreeing on the same layout. The `0xF` test is a literal `cmp dword ptr [ebx], 0xf`. Shown wrong by the copy length not being 0x104, or by MakeScope reading a fourth field of the spec.

addresses.name: CContextTrigger::CContextTrigger
addresses.no_signature: `ret 0x108` - the 0x104-byte scope specification is passed **by value** on the stack, which no C declaration Ghidra accepts can express alongside the 4-byte pointer argument beside it. `this` is in ESI, and ESI comes back as the return.
addresses.comment:
**The only constructor of CContextTrigger, and where the 0x150-byte object comes from.** 0x5D14A0 to the single `ret 0x108` at 0x5D1524. One caller, CTrigger::LoadKey at 0x5CAED7, which `operator new`s 0x150 bytes and pushes the 0x104-byte spec by value immediately before.

It inlines CTrigger's own constructor - `+4 = 0x18D`, the CTrigger vftable (VA 0x15C34DC), the child list cleared at `+8`/`+0xC`/`+0x10`, a byte at `+0x14`, a word at `+0x18`, **two 0x10-byte members built at `+0x1C` and `+0x2C`** through MSVC's `__ehvec_ctor` (rva 0x796170) with element constructor rva 0x9DB0 and destructor rva 0xC480, and a byte at `+0x3C` - then overwrites slot 0 with CContextTrigger's own table (VA 0x15F7CB4) and copies the spec into `+0x40` with EventScopeSpec_Construct.

0x40 + 0x110 = 0x150, so the spec is the whole of CContextTrigger's own data and the class has no other field.

The two members at `+0x1C` and `+0x2C` are each zeroed over three dwords and destroyed by a body that frees a linked list, so they are containers; **none of the four Evaluate bodies reads either**, so they are not an evaluation cache. What does read them was not found.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x9D14A0..0x9D1524. `image.findValue(0x15F7CB4)` returns exactly one site, 0x9D150A, inside this body - so this is the only constructor. The 0x150 is the literal `push 0x150` at 0x5CAEA6 in the only caller. Shown wrong by a second writer of that vftable constant, or by `ret 0x108` being anything else.

addresses.name: EventScopeUnknownKey
addresses.comment: The default arm of CEventScope::MakeScope's token switch, and the **only** writer of `CEventScope::unknown_context (+0x3D)`: `mov byte ptr [esp+0x75], cl` with `cl == 1`. It then falls into the empty-candidate arm at 0x5C1F34, which also clears `resolved (+0x3C)`. Reached for every key the switch does not recognise and the spec could not turn into a literal country tag.
addresses.evidence: `[esp+0x75]` on this frame is the local scope at [esp+0x38] plus 0x3D. A scan of the whole body finds no other write to that byte, and the constructor writes it as the high half of `mov word [eax+0x3c], 1`, i.e. zero. Shown wrong by a second writer anywhere.

addresses.name: EventScopeNoCandidate
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [esp+0x74], 0` - the **only** writer that clears `CEventScope::resolved (+0x3C)`, reached when the candidate vector CEventScope::MakeScope built is empty. That happens for `ally` on a country with an empty list, for `local_enemy` in a province with no qualifying unit, and for every unrecognised key, which arrives here through the default arm at 0x5C1F01. It is the byte CContextTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D154D) and CContextTrigger::WalkChildren (0x5D248D) test before doing anything, and that two of the three effect-side callers of MakeScope test as well (0x59E2CD, 0x59E33C). CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation, CContextTrigger::GetBlockText and the caller at 0x59E635 do not.
addresses.evidence: `[esp+0x74]` is the local scope + 0x3C on this frame, and [esp+0x44] in CContextTrigger::Evaluate is its local scope + 0x3C - the same field. Shown wrong by another writer of +0x3C, or by a gate reading a different offset.

addresses.name: TriggerLoadKeyScopeTest
addresses.comment:
**The seam between the grammar and the evaluator**, inside CTrigger::LoadKey's default arm: `cmp byte ptr [eax+0x3d], 0; sete al`. A key that is none of the 152 trigger keywords is turned into a scope specification (EventScopeSpec_Construct at 0x5CAE72), tried against a throwaway CEventScope built at 0x5CAE82, and **only if `unknown_context (+0x3D)` is still zero** does the loader `operator new(0x150)` a CContextTrigger for it (0x5CAEA6) rather than reporting a parse error through `trigger.cpp` at 0x5CAEEE.

This is why `CContextTrigger` has 10,974 live instances while `findings/FINDINGS-script.md` could place only 2 of its 153 keys: its keys are not in CTrigger::LoadKey's table at all - they are whatever CEventScope::MakeScope recognises, which is ten tokens plus any country tag plus any number. It is also the only reader of `+0x3D` in the image.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x5CAE62..0x5CAEE3 in context. The `je 0x9CAEE3` at 0x5CAEA4 goes to the error path that builds the string 'trigger.cpp' (VA 0x15F5DAC); the fall-through is the CContextTrigger construction. Shown wrong by a second reader of +0x3D, or by the 0x150 allocation belonging to something else - `image.findValue(0x15F7CB4)` says the constructor it calls is CContextTrigger's only one.

struct_fields.name: random_state
struct_fields.comment: **The scope's own random number state**, advanced in place. CEventScope's constructor (rva 0x5C1610) sets it from its EDX argument - the same value it puts in `seed` at +0x2C - and CEventScope::MakeScope passes `&scope->+8` to the LCG at rva 0x6A2E90, which reads the state, runs two steps of the MSVC `rand` recurrence (0x343FD / 0x269EC3) and writes the new state back before returning a 30-bit value. That is what picks the country for an `ally = { ... }` or `local_enemy = { ... }` context, so **those two contexts are deterministic given the scope's seed and advance it as a side effect**. The copy constructor copies it, so a rebound scope starts from wherever the parent had got to and advances its own copy.
struct_fields.evidence: `lea edx, [esi+8]; call 0xAA2E90` at 0x5C1F14, where esi is the receiver scope; 0xAA2E90 is `mov eax,[edx]` ... `mov [edx],eax`, so the pointer is the state. The constructor writes +8 and +0xC from EDX, and two call sites (0x4B9A99, 0x5769A0) set EDX from a call to 0xAA2F80 immediately before. Shown wrong by 0xAA2E90 not writing through its EDX argument.

struct_fields.name: country_tag
struct_fields.comment: The three letters and a NUL of the `country` CCountryTag whose id half the record already has at +0x14. CEventScope::SaveContents (rva 0x5C1690) writes it as the `country` key by taking `strlen` of this address and making a string of it; CEventScope::LoadKey writes it and +0x14 together from CCountryDataBase::GetTag. The constructor sets it to `0x2D2D2D`, `"---"`.
struct_fields.evidence: `lea ecx, [edi+0x10]` then an inline strlen then `SaveWriteKey(0x24D)` at 0x5C16BC-0x5C16F6, and token 0x24D is `country` in ghidra/saveTokens.json. The loader half writes [esi+0x10] and [esi+0x14] from the two dwords GetTag returns. Shown wrong by the save writing a number here rather than a string.

struct_fields.name: from_country_tag
struct_fields.comment: The letters of the **FROM** country, saved and loaded under the key `from_country` (token 0x61B); the id half is at +0x1C. The constructor sets it to `"---"`. CEventScope::MakeScope's `from` arm (token 0x34F) copies this pair into the new scope's `country`, which is what `FROM = { ... }` resolves to.
struct_fields.evidence: `lea ecx, [edi+0x18]`, inline strlen, `SaveWriteKey(0x61B)` at 0x5C176B-0x5C17A5; token 0x61B is `from_country`. LoadKey's 0x61B case writes +0x18/+0x1C from GetTag. MakeScope reads [esi+0x18]/[esi+0x1C] at 0x5C1DAD. Three readings agreeing.

struct_fields.name: from_country_id
struct_fields.comment: Id half of the tag at +0x18, and the field SaveContents guards the `from_country` key on - a zero here means FROM has no country and the key is not written at all.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp dword ptr [edi+0x1c], 0; je` around the whole `from_country` block at 0x5C1765. Same shape as the `country` guard on +0x14, which the record already names.

struct_fields.name: rebel_faction_type
struct_fields.comment: First half of the `{ type = N id = N }` object reference saved under the key `rebel_faction` (token 0x644). CEventScope::LoadKey reads it with **ParseObjectId** (rva 0x67B250) given `scope + 0x20`, which is the same call CReferenceObject::LoadKey makes with `this + 8` and the reason CMinister keeps `id_type` at 0x8 and `id` at 0xC; SaveContents writes the pair back through rva 0x6789F0. So a scope can be about a rebel faction as well as a country and a province, and nothing in the evaluation half read here ever looks at it.
struct_fields.evidence: `add esi, 0x20; push esi; push parse; call 0xA7B250` at 0x5C19F9 under token 0x644, and 0xA7B250 is the recorded ParseObjectId. SaveContents guards on `+0x20 != 0 || +0x24 != 0` and passes `lea eax, [edi+0x20]`. Shown wrong by ParseObjectId writing one int rather than two.

struct_fields.name: rebel_faction_id
struct_fields.comment: Second half of the object reference at +0x20 - the id ParseObjectId writes into `pair[1]`.
struct_fields.evidence: ParseObjectId's recorded signature is `(CParseContext*, int* pair)` writing two ints, and SaveContents tests `[edi+0x24]` beside `[edi+0x20]` in the same guard at 0x5C1814-0x5C181E.

struct_fields.name: province
struct_fields.comment: **The province the scope is about**, saved and loaded under the key `province` (token 0x1EE). Everything that resolves a scope indexes a province array with it: CEventScope::MakeScope uses `g_CMap (0x1A8557C) + 0x2200` for the `owner`, `controller`, `sea_zone` and `local_enemy` contexts, and EventScope_GetCountryTag uses `g_CCurrentGameState (0x1A89790) + 0xB8C` to fall back on the province's owner when the scope names no country. Zero means the scope is not about a province; the constructor leaves it so, and every context that sets a country clears it.
struct_fields.evidence: `SaveWriteKey(0x1EE)` on `[edi+0x28]` at 0x5C171D-0x5C1725 and token 0x1EE is `province`; the matching LoadKey case writes +0x28 from atoi. Five independent readers index a province array with it. Shown wrong by any of those reads being a different offset.

struct_fields.name: seed
struct_fields.comment: The random seed the scope was built with, saved under the key `seed` (token 0x356) - the only one of the six keys SaveContents writes **unconditionally**. The constructor puts its EDX argument here and in the live state at +8 and +0xC, and at two of the call sites inspected that argument comes straight out of the generator at rva 0x6A2F80. So this is the seed as recorded and +8 is the state as it stands.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov edi, [edi+0x2c]; SaveWriteKey(0x356)` at 0x5C1835 with no guard around it, and token 0x356 is `seed`. The constructor writes +8, +0xC and +0x2C all from EDX. Shown wrong by the key being written under a guard, or by +0x2C being advanced anywhere.

struct_fields.name: from_province
struct_fields.comment: The **FROM** province, saved and loaded under the key `from_province` (token 0x61C). CEventScope::MakeScope's `from` arm copies it into the new scope's `province`, beside the `from_country` pair.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov ebx, [edi+0x30]; test; SaveWriteKey(0x61C)` at 0x5C17CC-0x5C17D9, token 0x61C is `from_province`, and MakeScope reads `[esi+0x30]` into the new scope's +0x28 at 0x5C1DB3. Three readings agreeing.

struct_fields.name: this_scope
struct_fields.comment: **The scope the event was raised with - what `this = { ... }` means.** The constructor sets it to `this`, so it is never null and for an unrebound scope points at the scope itself; CEventScope::CopyConstruct copies the pointer verbatim, so every scope a context rebinds **still points at the original**. Two readers: CEventScope::MakeScope's `this` arm (token 0x377) takes the country and province off it, and EventScope_GetCountryTag (rva 0x5C1A40) resolves "which country is this scope about" through it rather than off the scope directly. Not saved.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov dword ptr [eax+0x38], eax` at 0x5C1671 in the constructor; `mov edx, [ecx+0x38]; mov [eax+0x38], edx` in the copy constructor; `mov esi, [esi+0x38]` at 0x5C1DC7 under token 0x377 (`this`); `mov eax, [eax+0x38]` at 0x5C1A5B. Shown wrong by a writer other than the constructor and the copy, which would make the pointer mean something narrower than 'the original scope'.

struct_fields.name: resolved
struct_fields.comment: **Did this scope resolve to anything.** 1 at construction (`mov word ptr [eax+0x3c], 1`, which sets this byte and clears +0x3D) and cleared in exactly one place, 0x5C1F34 in CEventScope::MakeScope, when the candidate list for an `ally` or `local_enemy` context came up empty or the key was not a context at all. CContextTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D154D) and CContextTrigger::WalkChildren (0x5D248D) test it and do nothing when it is 0 - so **an unresolvable scope makes the block false rather than raising anything** - and so do two of the three effect-side callers of MakeScope, at 0x59E2CD and 0x59E33C. CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation and CContextTrigger::GetBlockText do **not** test it, which is a real asymmetry between the tooltip's tally and the answer.
struct_fields.evidence: One writer (0x5C1F34) and four gates (0x5D154D, 0x5D248D, 0x59E2CD, 0x59E33C) read instruction by instruction; the two CContextTrigger gates read `cmp byte ptr [esp+0x44], 0` off a local whose base is [esp+8], i.e. +0x3C. Shown wrong by a second clear, or by any of the three gates reading a different byte.

struct_fields.name: unknown_context
struct_fields.comment: **Was the key not a scope keyword at all.** 0 at construction, set to 1 only by the default arm of CEventScope::MakeScope's token switch (0x5C1F01), and read in exactly one place in the image: CTrigger::LoadKey at 0x5CAE9B, which makes a CContextTrigger for an otherwise unknown trigger key only while this is still 0. So the flag is the whole of how the grammar decides whether something like `owner`, `GER` or `64` is a scope rather than a parse error - and the ten tokens CEventScope::MakeScope knows, plus any country tag and any number, are the complete list of CContextTrigger's keys.
struct_fields.evidence: One writer (0x5C1F01) and one reader (0x5CAE9B), both read in context; `[esp+0x75]` in MakeScope's frame is the local scope + 0x3D, and the reader is `cmp byte ptr [eax+0x3d], 0` on MakeScope's return value. Shown wrong by a second reader, which would mean the flag is consulted at evaluation time too.

slots_noted: CTrigger slots 10 and 11 (rva 0x5D0680 and 0x5D06C0) are deliberately NOT recorded here. project.json already carries both under vftable_slots.CTrigger, and mergeFindings inserts slot entries textually at the head of the class's block - so a second "10" would become a duplicate JSON key that loses to the existing one, silently. The slot-10 signature in that block has the arguments in the wrong order and needs the hand edit described in the comment on 0x5D0680. Both bodies sit in more than eight tables (143 and 153) and every holder derives from CTrigger, so that is inheritance rather than a linker fold.
